summary: Bradford's Instagram content presents housing as a central, sustained focus. Bradford frames Toronto as facing a housing affordability and starts crisis, citing figures such as 68 to 90 percent drops in housing starts, development charges rising over 1,000 percent since 2010, and roughly 30 percent of unit costs coming from taxes and fees (DR5QW7XEnaA, DRzoVv0DUq0, DJEbmKVtRhs). Bradford supports cutting development charges (including a 25 percent reduction motion), streamlining approvals, ending exclusionary zoning, legalizing multiplexes and sixplexes, permitting garden and laneway suites, single-egress stairs, modular and rapid-build construction, mid-rise on Avenues, and office-to-residential conversions (CsFNxk8N7cZ, DLV5wxxMq3u, CIjHtg6hSYJ, DHJ9qe-yi5e, C7U90-KvQUv). Bradford also supports supportive housing with wraparound services, Inclusionary Zoning, purpose-built rental incentives, doubling the first-time homebuyer rebate, and a vacant home tax, while opposing added housing taxes and the current Vacant Home Tax reverse-onus design (DQwumxDjYhU, CWEjlp8gxH4, DSabj0Mjkvw, DA_PG3-Rmwz).

key_positions.stance: Supports cutting development charges and municipal fees to spur housing construction, including a proposed 25 percent reduction on condos and 100 percent on affordable and purpose-built rental.
Supports ending exclusionary zoning and legalizing missing middle housing (multiplexes, sixplexes, garden suites, laneway suites) across Toronto neighbourhoods.
Supports streamlining approvals, cutting red tape, and using modular and rapid-build construction to accelerate housing delivery.
Supports supportive housing with wraparound mental health, addiction, and job training services as the long-term response to homelessness.
Supports allowing mid-rise apartments and higher unit caps on Avenues and major streets, including raising the major-streets cap from 30 to 60 units.
Opposes adding new taxes on housing including the luxury home tax and characterizes the current Vacant Home Tax's reverse-onus design as flawed.
Supports Inclusionary Zoning requiring up to 22 percent affordability in areas across Toronto.
Supports purpose-built rental housing, including federal GST removal and low-cost financing, and opposes affordable-housing requirements described as making projects financially unviable.
Supports doubling the first-time homebuyer rebate and raising the threshold from $400,000 to $750,000.
Supports converting underutilized office space into housing.
Opposes Mayor Chow's public builder approach as bureaucratic and ineffective at delivering results.
